game.name: babel
game.description: Babel: an emergent-language referential game for four cogs. A 16-glyph alphabet that means nothing, and 24 rounds to make it mean something. Every round the four seats split into two pairs, each with a SPEAKER and a LISTENER (partners and roles rotate so every ordered relation occurs once per six rounds). The speaker sees a target scene - a shape (circle, square, triangle, star), a colour (red, blue, green, yellow), and a count (1-4) - and sends a message of 1 to 8 glyphs. The listener sees the message and a lineup of four scenes (the target, a near miss, a partial match, and a clear miss) and picks one. Both score when the pick is right. Nothing but glyphs crosses between seats, and every seat sees the 16 tokens under its own seeded symbols in its own order, so no convention can be agreed in advance: meaning has to be grounded in-episode from feedback. Each seat keeps private notes the game returns every round. Seats play under anonymous cog aliases. Scripted, prompt, and Jev policies choose actions in ordinary player containers; the game owns visibility, legality, results, and replay.

tokens.description: One connection token per player slot, indexed by slot.

players.description: One player display-name object per seat, indexed by slot.

num_agents.description: Seat count; injected by the commissioner. Babel is a four-player game.

seed.description: Pins the alphabet, every seat's view of it, the pairing schedule with its targets and lineups, the seat aliases, and the baseline's tie-breaks. Omit for a fresh random seed per episode.

rounds.description: Rounds in the episode (capped by the model-call budget: four calls per round). Every seat plays every round.

episodeTimeoutSeconds.description: Wall-clock the game assumes the platform allows an episode when COWORLD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is not in its environment; play stops after the current round at 60% of it so results and the replay always land.

decisionTimeoutSeconds.description: Maximum time for one player action before game fallback.

names.description: Policy display names, indexed by slot. Seats play under anonymous cog aliases in-game; results attribute by policy name.

scores.description: Share of the seat's rounds (either role) in which the listener picked the target: correct / rounds played, 0..1.

correct.description: Successful rounds the seat was in, as speaker or listener.

asSpeaker.description: Successful rounds in which the seat was the speaker.

asListener.description: Successful rounds in which the seat was the listener.

maxRounds.description: The episode's round count after budget fitting.

reason.description: How the episode ended: complete (all rounds played) or deadline (episode clock; scores use the rounds played).

player.value: babel.player.v2 uses JSON text frames on COWORLD_PLAYER_WS_URL. The game sends welcome, redacted state, private decision, and final frames. Each decision has a unique id, acting slot, role, partner alias, that seat's 16 visible glyphs, private notes, and completed feedback from only its own pair. A speaker sees target scene id (shape*16+colour*4+count-1), never the lineup. A listener sees its partner's message in its own glyphs and four scene ids, never the target. The player returns {"type":"action","protocol":"babel.player.v2","id":N,"action":{"tokens":["glyph",...],"notes":"..."},"source":"scripted"|"llm"|"fallback"} for a speaker, or action {"pick":0..3,"notes":"..."} for a listener. Messages have 1 to 8 glyphs from that seat's alphabet; notes are truncated to 600 runes. The game validates actions, maps glyphs to token ids, applies speak/pick, and uses its scripted baseline on missing or invalid replies. Model prompts, calls, and Jev rankings stay in the player container; the game receives no model secret.

global.value: Global spectators connect a websocket to /global and receive the full snapshot as JSON after every event: {"type":"state","game":"babel","seats":[{name,score,correct,asSpeaker,asListener,role,partner,notes}],"round":int,"rounds":int,"roundsPlayed":int,"glyphs":[16 canonical glyphs],"perm":[4][16],"pairs":[{speaker,listener,target,lineup[4],tokens|null,pick|null,correct|null}],"phase":speak0|pick0|speak1|pick1|between|done,"gameDone":bool,"reason":str,"policyNames":[...],"events":[{kind:start|round|speak|pick|end,...}],"started":bool,"done":bool,"connected":[bool]}. Scene ids are shape*16+colour*4+count (0..63). The events array is append-only and carries the complete transcript, including every seat's notes. The browser page at /client/global renders the stage; /client/replay plays a recorded episode; the static replay viewer bundle renders replays hosted by the platform (index.html?replay=<url>).

readme.value: Babel is a four-player emergent-language game. Each round has two speaker/listener pairs; a speaker sends 1 to 8 glyphs from a private alphabet and a listener chooses one of four scenes. Each player receives only its private task and own feedback, then submits an ordinary action. Scripted, prompt, and Jev policies run in player containers. The game owns visibility, validation, results, and replay and falls back to its code-and-decode baseline on missing or invalid actions.

content.value:
# Babel rules

- Four seats. Every round the seats split into two pairs, each with a SPEAKER and a LISTENER. Round r (0-based) uses the matching M[r mod 3] of {(0,1),(2,3)}, {(0,2),(1,3)}, {(0,3),(1,2)}; within a pair the first seat speaks when (r div 3) mod 2 == 0, otherwise the second. Every ordered speaker->listener relation occurs once per six rounds.
- A scene is a shape (circle, square, triangle, star), a colour (red, blue, green, yellow), and a count (1-4); scene id = shape*16 + colour*4 + (count-1).
- Per pair per round the seed draws a target and a lineup of four scenes: the target, a near miss (shares two attributes), a partial (shares one), and a clear miss (shares none), shuffled and labelled A-D. The speaker sees only the target; the listener sees the message and the lineup.
- The message is 1 to 8 tokens from a 16-token alphabet. Each seat sees the tokens under its own seeded symbols in its own order; glyph identity never survives the channel, only token identity does. Nothing else crosses between seats.
- After the pick both pair members learn the target, the pick, and the verdict. Each seat's prompt carries its own history (never the other pair's) and its latest private notes (up to 600 characters, overwritten when a reply carries notes, kept when it does not). Notes are recorded in the event log for spectators.
- The episode runs `rounds` rounds (default 24, capped to 60 by the model-call budget); the episode clock may end it early after the current round.

## Scoring

A round-pair succeeds when the listener picks the target. A seat's `correct` is its successes in the rounds it was in (either role); `score = correct / rounds played`. Results also report `asSpeaker` and `asListener` successes. Fully cooperative; the league ranks seats by mean episode score.

## The meta

Each player policy receives its own alphabet, notes, feedback, and target (speaker) or message and lineup (listener), then submits an ordinary action to the game. Prompts that invent a consistent compositional code (one glyph per attribute value), keep a per-partner dictionary in their notes, and prefer the near-miss reading when unsure tend to score; the built-in scripted baseline (fixed three-token code as speaker, count-based association decoder as listener) fills seats without prompts, is a fieldable policy in its own right, and is the consistent-convention partner a prompt has to adapt to.

player.name: Babel Prompt Player
player.description: Reference prompt policy: the player calls Claude with its private observation and PLAYER_PROMPT, then submits glyphs or a lineup pick through babel.player.v2.

player.name: Babel Scripted Coder
player.description: Scripted code-and-decode policy in the player: fixed shape/colour/count glyph code as speaker, association decoder as listener.

player.name: Babel Jev Player
player.description: Jev ranks legal speaker glyphs and listener scene picks from the player's private babel.player.v2 observation.

variants.name: Standard game
variants.description: Four cogs, a fresh 16-glyph alphabet, 24 rounds (budget-fitted); every ordered speaker-listener relation four times.
